questions.question: Five identical red balls and four identical blue balls are arranged in a row at random. What is the probability that no two blue balls are placed together?
questions.title: 5 red + 4 blue balls in a row — no two blue together

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Total ways to place the 4 blue balls among 9 positions = C(9,4) = 126.
Favorable: arrange 5 red balls first, creating 6 gaps (before, between, after) — choose 4 of these 6 gaps for the blue balls so no two are adjacent = C(6,4) = 15.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red, 5 yellow, and 6 green balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random, what is the probability that none of them is green?

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 4 red, 5 yellow, 6 green (15 total). Draw 3.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Favorable = choose all 3 from non-green (9 balls) = C(9,3) = 84. Total = C(15,3) = 455.
84/455 = 12/65 (dividing by 7).

questions.question: The letters of the word 'SOCIETY' are arranged at random in a row. What is the probability that the three vowels come in even places?
questions.title: SOCIETY — vowels in even places

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
SOCIETY has 7 distinct letters; vowels O, I, E (3), consonants S, C, T, Y (4). Even positions among 1–7 are 2, 4, 6 (exactly 3 slots).
Favorable = (ways to arrange 3 vowels in the 3 even slots) × (ways to arrange 4 consonants in remaining slots) = 3! × 4!.
Total arrangements = 7!.

questions.question: Two players A and B toss a standard fair coin alternately, with player A going first. The first player to successfully get a Head wins the game. What is the absolute probability that player B wins the match?
questions.title: Coin-tossing game — probability B wins

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A and B alternate, A first; first Head wins. Let p = P(B wins).

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: P(A wins on 1st toss) = 1/2. If both A and B miss their first attempts (prob 1/4), the game effectively restarts with B now "waiting" — giving the recursive relation p = (1/2)(1/2) + (1/4)p → p = 1/4 + p/4 → (3/4)p = 1/4.

3024/6561 simplifies (÷27) to 112/243.

questions.question: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. Given that the absolute sum of the resulting numbers is a prime number, what is the conditional probability that at least one of the dice shows a 3?
questions.title: Two dice — P(at least one die shows 3 | sum is prime)

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Prime sums possible: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Count outcomes (out of 36) for each: sum2→1, sum3→2, sum5→4, sum7→6, sum11→2. Total prime-sum outcomes = 15.
Among these, outcomes containing at least one 3: from sum5 → (2,3),(3,2); from sum7 → (3,4),(4,3) = 4 outcomes. (sum3, sum2, sum11 outcomes contain no 3.)

questions.question: A trained marksman has an independent success probability of 0.8 for hitting a target. What is the absolute minimum number of shots he must fire to ensure the probability of hitting the target at least once is strictly greater than 0.99?
questions.title: Minimum shots for P(at least one hit) > 0.99 (p=0.8 per shot)

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
P(at least one hit in n shots) = 1 − (0.2)ⁿ. Need 1 − 0.2ⁿ > 0.99 → 0.2ⁿ < 0.01.
Check: 0.2² = 0.04 (fails), 0.2³ = 0.008 (< 0.01, succeeds).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Minimum **3 shots** (giving P ≈ 0.992 > 0.99).

questions.question: A three-digit number is formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition. What is the probability that the number is greater than 400?
questions.title: 3-digit number from {0,1,2,3,4,5}, no repetition — probability > 400

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Total 3-digit numbers (first digit ≠ 0): 5 (first digit choices) × 5 (second, including 0) × 4 (third) = 100.
For the number to exceed 400, the first digit must be 4 or 5 (any arrangement starting with 4 or 5 automatically exceeds 400 since digits can't repeat to form exactly "400").
First digit = 4: remaining 2 digits chosen/arranged from {0,1,2,3,5} → 5 × 4 = 20 numbers. First digit = 5: similarly 20 numbers.
Favorable = 20 + 20 = 40.

sections.content:
Sum is even if both numbers are odd or both are even (10 odd, 10 even numbers).
Favorable = C(10,2) + C(10,2) = 45 + 45 = 90. Total = C(20,2) = 190.

questions.question: Bag A contains 3 red and 4 black balls. Bag B contains 4 red and 5 black balls. One ball is transferred from Bag A to Bag B, and then a ball is drawn from Bag B. What is the probability that the drawn ball is red?
questions.title: Ball transferred between bags, then drawn — probability red

sections.label: Given
sections.content:
Bag A: 3 red, 4 black (7 total). Bag B: 4 red, 5 black (9 total). Transfer 1 ball A→B, then draw from B.
**Steps (Law of Total Probability):**
- P(transfer red) = 3/7 → Bag B becomes 5 red, 5 black (10 total) → P(draw red | transferred red) = 5/10 = 1/2.
- P(transfer black) = 4/7 → Bag B becomes 4 red, 6 black (10 total) → P(draw red | transferred black) = 4/10 = 2/5.
P(red) = (3/7)(1/2) + (4/7)(2/5) = 3/14 + 8/35 = 15/70 + 16/70.
